t: Chinese estimates and Japanese claims of losses differ widely: China's official report of 5 November gave 187,200 killed and wounded, Japanese estimates were roughly 250,000, and the Japanese gave their own as 9,115 killed and 31,257 injured.

The Japanese expected to take Shanghai within days, but the Chinese held out for over three months, and Chiang Kai-shek lost much of his best-trained army, including some 10,000 of the 25,000 junior officers trained at Whampoa between 1929 and 1937.
Historian Peter Harmsen holds that the battle presaged urban combat as it was to be waged throughout the rest of the twentieth century; it was the largest urban battle before Stalingrad.
dyk: A Chinese air attack on the Japanese flagship Izumo on 14 August 1937 went wrong, and bombs fell on the Shanghai International Settlement; the day became known as Black Saturday.
ev: Two Japanese naval personnel and a Chinese guard are found dead at Hongqiao Airport, and the Japanese begin sending reinforcements to Shanghai
Fighting begins between Chinese and Japanese forces in Zhabei, Wusong and Jiangwan, and on 14 August China declares its resistance to Japanese aggression
The 36th Division's attack towards the Huangpu docks pushes the Japanese back but cannot break through
The Japanese 3rd and 11th Divisions land on the northeast coast, lengthening the front
Baoshan falls on 6 September, and the Chinese hold Luodian for weeks at heavy cost
The fight for Wusong Creek and Dachang ends with Dachang's fall on 26 October, and the Chinese withdraw from the city's urban centre
The Japanese 10th Army lands at Jinshanwei on 5 November, and on 8 November the Chinese order a general retreat
The Wufu Line is penetrated on 19 November and the Xicheng Line given up on 26 November, and the fighting runs on to Nanjing

f.date: 13 August to 26 November 1937, in three stages: 13 to 22 August, 23 August to 26 October, and 27 October to the end of November
f.place: Shanghai and its surroundings: the city's districts, the creek country to the north, the coast of the Yangtze delta and Hangzhou Bay, China
f.sides: The Republic of China under Chiang Kai-shek, with commanders including Zhang Zhizhong and Chen Cheng; the Empire of Japan, with the Shanghai Expeditionary Army under Iwane Matsui. The battle eventually involved around one million troops. In early October the Japanese had more than 200,000 troops in the region against over 700,000 Chinese deployed across a wide front.
f.outcome: The Japanese captured Shanghai after more than three months of fighting on land, in the air and at sea. China lost a significant portion of its best troops and no foreign power intervened.
